newsitem.title: INDIA: India says talks with Pakistan to start June 19.
newsitem.headline: India says talks with Pakistan to start June 19.

text.p: Senior foreign ministry officials from India and Pakistan will meet in Islamabad for talks from June 19 to 23, India's Foreign Ministry said on Friday.

The talks between the neighbours' foreign secretaries, their seniormost career diplomats, will follow a rare meeting between their prime ministers in May and an earlier round of negotiations in March, which ended a tense three-year stand-off.
"The next round of foreign secretary-level talks will be held in Islamabad from June 19 to 23," a Foreign Ministry statement said.
Pakistan on Thursday accused India of raising tension ahead of the talks, a charge New Delhi promptly denied.

Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan cited a recent alleged violation of Pakistani airspace, the reported deployment of Indian medium-range ballistic missiles near the border and a border clash on Tuesday night.

An Indian Foreign Ministry spokesman reiterated New Delhi's denial that one of its jet fighters had flown over Pakistan earlier this month, breaking the sound barrier and rattling windows in Islamabad.
He also noted Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's statement on Wednesday denying that India had deployed ballistic missiles near to the border with Pakistan.
As for any border clash, the Foreign Ministry spokesman said: "India has been subjected to unprovoked firing on several occasions across the border".
The two countries have fought three wars since 1947, two of them over the divided Himalayan region of Kashmir. The last round of talks in January 1994 derailed over Kashmir.

India controls two-thirds of Kashmir and Pakistan the rest. New Delhi accuses its Islamic neighbour of arming and training Moslem rebels in the region. Islamabad says it provides only moral and diplomatic support to the rebels.
Pakistan says Kashmir is the core issue that the neighbours must resolve, while India says it is keen to make progress in other areas such as trade.

Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif last week said he sought a "new beginning" with India. Gujral recently said he felt that both countries now understood that hostile bilateral ties were harming them.
